subject: general
question: 44 pipes can fill a large water tank in 27 hours. How many hours will it take for 66 pipes to fill four such tanks?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the chain rule formula: M₁ × H₁ / W₁ = M₂ × H₂ / W₂

⇒ 44 × 27 / 1 = 66 × H₂ / 4

⇒ H₂ = (44 × 27 × 4) ÷ 66

⇒ H₂ = 72

**∴ The correct answer is 72 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of pipes (M₁) = 44

Time to fill 1 tank (H₁) = 27 hours

New number of pipes (M₂) = 66

Number of tanks to fill (W₂) = 4

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken by 44 pipes to fill 1 tank = 27 hours

⇒ Total time taken by 1 pipe to fill 1 tank = 44 × 27 = 1188 hours

⇒ Time taken by 66 pipes to fill 1 tank = 1188 ÷ 66 = 18 hours

⇒ Time taken by 66 pipes to fill 4 such tanks = 18 × 4 = 72 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 72 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method in Time & Work

If more resources (pipes) are used, less time is taken to do the same amount of work (Inverse Proportion). If more work (tanks) is done, more time is taken (Direct Proportion).

MDH Formula

A direct shortcut to compare two scenarios of work: (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂, where M is workers or identical machines, and W is the total work done.

Pipes & Cisterns

All pipes of identical size fill a tank at the exact same rate. Their combined efficiency is directly proportional to the total number of active pipes.
